serp-preview.privacyNote: This tool runs 100% in your browser. Your data never leaves your device.
serp-preview.name: SERP Preview
serp-preview.tagline: Preview your Google search snippet live.
serp-preview.metaTitle: SERP Preview - See Your Google Snippet Before Publishing | JaurTools
serp-preview.metaDescription: Preview how your title and meta description look in Google results on desktop and mobile. Live character counts — free.
serp-preview.keywords: serp preview, google snippet preview, meta title checker, search result preview, seo snippet tool
serp-preview.quickAnswer: This tool shows how your page will appear in Google search results. Type your title tag, URL, and meta description to see a realistic preview with live character counters: titles over about 60 characters and descriptions over about 155 characters risk being cut off with an ellipsis.
keyFacts: Google typically shows around 50-60 characters of a title and 150-160 of a description, measured in pixels.
Titles are truncated by pixel width, not exact character count; wide letters like W take more space.
Google may rewrite your title or description if it thinks other page content fits the query better.
The favicon and site name shown come from your site settings, not the meta tags.
A clear, honest snippet improves click-through rate without tricking users.
howTo: Type the title tag of your page (aim for 60 characters or fewer).
Enter the page URL to preview the site name and breadcrumb.
Write the meta description (aim for 155 characters or fewer).
Switch between desktop and mobile preview widths.
Copy the generated title and meta tags into your page HTML.
serp-preview.formula:
Title limit: ~60 characters (600px)
Description limit: ~155 characters
Example title (47 chars): "Free Online Tools - No Signup Needed | JaurTools"
Example description (118 chars): "Use 600+ free browser-based tools..."
serp-preview.workedExample:
Title: "Free Online Tools - No Signup Needed | JaurTools" (47 characters) — under the 60-character guide, so it shows fully.
Description: "Use 600+ free browser-based tools: calculators, converters, PDF tools and more. No signup, no downloads, 100% private." (118 characters) — under 155, so no truncation.
A 90-character title would show an ellipsis around character 60 on desktop results.
benefits: See truncation problems before you publish.
Live counters keep titles and descriptions in range.
Mobile preview matches how most users search today.
One click copies clean title and meta tags.
limitations: Limits are guidelines; Google measures in pixels, not characters.
Google often rewrites snippets, so the preview is not a guarantee.
Non-Latin scripts (Hindi, Arabic) use different widths per character.
This previews one organic result style; rich results and ads differ.

faqs.q: Why was my title cut off in real results?
faqs.a: Google truncates by pixel width. Even under 60 characters, many wide letters can overflow. Shorten the title or move key words earlier.

faqs.q: Does Google always use my meta description?
faqs.a: No. Google rewrites descriptions in most cases, pulling text it thinks matches the query. A good description still raises your chances of being used.

faqs.q: How long should a meta description be?
faqs.a: Aim for 150-155 characters. Longer text gets cut with an ellipsis; much shorter text wastes the space Google gives you.
They can stand out but Google often strips or ignores them, and they look unprofessional for many topics. Use sparingly if at all.
It approximates the narrower mobile card width. Real rendering also depends on device, font size settings, and result features on the page.

serp-preview.assumptionNote: Character limits are pixel-based approximations. Google may rewrite titles and descriptions in live results.
